why: The item's own sentence: an exclusion nobody can see looks exactly like a file that was not there. Dropping the row hides the exclusion, and a reader checking whether their file was indexed finds no trace of it either way.

tag: an exclusion is recorded without the rule that caused it
why: A state with no basis is the shape this whole programme removes: a file reported EXCLUDED with no rule tells a reader their document is missing and not why, and they cannot tell a deliberate exclusion from a failure.

old:

new:
files.append({"path": rel, "state": INDEXED, "ext": ext, "needs": pkg,
                                  "basis": (f"NOT_READ: no extractor for {ext} in this deployment — "
why: This is the brief's ingestor restored: it would have reported ASSIMILATED over folders holding only formats it could not read. Neither extractor is installed here, so NOT_READ naming the missing package is the honest answer and the item says it must never be replaced by an optimistic one.

tag: an unread file's text reaches the search index
why: THE FU-124 RULE: nothing unread is in the knowledge base. A token entry for a file whose state is NOT_READ means search answers from a document nobody extracted — and the leg checks the stored token map directly, not just the search result.

tag: an oversized file is truncated and indexed anyway
why: A half-read file in a search index answers questions about a document nobody has. The leg writes a file comfortably over the cap and asserts its marker is unsearchable, so the cap has to be enforced rather than merely published.

tag: the published counts are read back instead of recounted
old: fresh = {s: sum(1 for f in files if f.get("state") == s) for s in (INDEXED, NOT_READ, EXCLUDED)}
why: The bar's words are that the counts MATCH A RE-COUNT. Returning the stored counts as the re-count makes the comparison trivially true — a check that cannot disagree with what it checks. The leg also recomputes the counts independently in the test, so the module's own recount is not the only witness.
